points.description: States that at each step the algorithm selects/identifies the minimum (smallest) element from the remaining unsorted elements. Accept equivalent wording such as 'finds the smallest of the rest' or 'picks the minimum from the unsorted part'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions finding the smallest/minimum element but does not make clear that it is chosen from the remaining unsorted elements.

levels.says: Mentions finding the smallest/minimum element, but does not make clear that it is selected from the remaining unsorted portion (for example, says only 'find the minimum of the array').

points.description: States that the selected minimum is swapped with the current element/position. Accept equivalent wording such as 'exchange it with the element being considered' or 'put the minimum in the current spot by swapping'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions swapping or placing the minimum at the current position but omits one side of the exchange.

levels.says: Mentions swapping or placing the minimum at the current position, but omits one side of the exchange (for example, says 'swap the minimum' without saying with what, or says 'put the minimum in place' without saying it is swapped).

points.description: States that the array is processed one element/position at a time, from left to right (in order). Accept equivalent wording such as 'go through the array from the start' or 'move through each position in turn'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says the array is processed element by element or in order but does not clearly state left-to-right/current-position progression.

levels.says: Says the array is processed element by element or in order, but does not clearly state left-to-right or current-position progression.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the central idea of repeatedly selecting the minimum from the remaining unsorted elements and swapping it into the current position while moving through the array from left to right. Part marks are given when one of these ideas is vague or missing, especially if the minimum is not clearly said to come from the remaining unsorted portion. No marks are given for describing a different sorting method or for an answer with no selection/minimum and swap idea.
